components.basis: All four listed subcomponents (GOAL-01 to GOAL-04) are supplied at their required standing: definitions on the route and proofs with written annex steps, for the full primitive propositional language and for finite first-order roots with and without equality. The original row's notes (absent book-wide apart from the many-valued matrix tableau; also listed in B3 automation and the cross-cutting list) add no hypothesis; target_home P2.2 is a placement field. No narrower claim is substituted: the finite-root hypothesis is stated in every result (body 21-36, 359-369, 660-700) and equality is treated, not excluded.

Rules: the seven expandable premise shapes of the full primitive language (bottom, not, and, or, implies; iff and verum are defined abbreviations at restoration/inherited-01661-01816.tex 48-58) with their linear or branching alternatives, terminal formulas p, not-p, bottom, not-bottom, one rule per expandable shape (body 66-94), and the same rules on sheet:tableaux-cpl (tableaux-cpl.tex 11-19, rendered by \showcalculus at classical-and-constructive-calculi.tex 204). Branches: a retained list with a set of marked positions, occurrences, expansion steps that append one child per alternative and delete nothing, tableaux as last members of expansion sequences, saturation and finished tableaux (body 95-133; propositional-hilbert-tableaux.tex 132-149). Closure: a branch closes on bottom or a complementary pair, a closed branch admits no step, a tableau is closed when every branch is (body 100-114; propositional-hilbert-tableaux.tex 138-142; sheet close rule). Input convention: root branch lists each member once, consequence rooted at Gamma plus not-phi with no simplification, validity rooted at not-phi (body 41-58). Worked closed and open examples and the unfinished-branch warning at body 267-317.

Root language L_Gamma, parameters a_n, a fixed computable enumeration of all closed L_Gamma^*-terms, the equality-free calculus T and the calculus with equality T^= (body 359-390; first-order-calculi-supplement.tex 114-135). Quantifier rules: delta steps (exists, not-forall) use the parameter of least index not occurring on the branch and are done once; gamma steps (forall, not-exists) are retained and available at every closed term, each use recorded as a task (body 418-457; sheet tableaux-fol.tex 23-26). Equality rules: premise-free reflexivity at every closed term and left-to-right replacement of one occurrence in an atomic sentence, each triple used at most once (body 392-416; sheet 27-28). Freshness, instantiation and fairness are stated as exact requirements (body 483-497; fairness over the whole enumeration at first-order-calculi-supplement.tex 127-129; saturation = every available task done, including reflexivity and replacement tasks, body 428-440 and 478-479), with the failure of each shown (unfair branch 777-788; non-fresh parameter 790-798) and a fair staged procedure (625-658).

Propositional: semantic case-split lemma, branch invariants, soundness of closure for every tableau, termination, truth lemma for the branch valuation of an open saturated branch, completeness and read-off, and the consequence/validity tests with countervaluations (body 152-234), each with written annex steps (annex 10-241); thm:p02-tableau-adequacy (propositional-hilbert-tableaux.tex 151-163) is proved from them at propositional-hilbert.tex 67-86. First-order, T and T^=: sound case splits including the fresh-parameter and equality cases, invariants incl. limit branches, soundness of closure (body 499-552; annex 325-454); Hintikka sets, quotient Herbrand structure, congruence, Herbrand truth lemma, open saturated finite or limit branches are Hintikka sets, countermodel extraction with reduct and expansion to L (body 554-623; annex 456-628); completeness via the fair systematic procedure, plus consequence/validity and countermodel (body 660-700; annex 630-760); thm:p02-fol-tableau-adequacy (first-order-calculi-supplement.tex 137-160) proved at annex 61-83. Results the proofs use (substitution lemma, reduct invariance, substitution complexity and free variables, unique readability) are proved on the route; no owed step is replaced by a citation.

Propositional: size measure, every step lowers it, explicit step bound, a step applies iff the tableau is not finished, and a procedure that halts on every input and decides satisfiability, consequence and validity (body 135-150, 186-202, 236-265; annex 123-162, 243-273). First-order: why termination fails and finite branches with a universal occurrence are never saturated (body 319-342; annex 275-299); the fair staged procedure halts with 'unsatisfiable' on exactly the unsatisfiable finite roots and, when it does not halt, a path with an open, saturated, infinite limit branch is constructed (clause 2, body 666-669; annex 649-702); {forall x Px} gives a satisfiable root on which it never halts (758-775); the decision versus semidecision boundary (800-816) uses the cited undecidability theorem only for its concluding remark, marked cited at inherited-08248-08305.tex 9-14.
